definition_zh: 高效的；能干的；有产生力的
definition_en: working well with little waste, organized and capable, or having the power to produce an effect
core_image: 一条流水线，零件进来，成品出去，地上没有剩料
scene: 换上新电机后，同样的活只用一半时间就干完了。The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
sceneCN: 这里 efficient 是「高效的」（第 1 个义项：以较少的投入完成同样的工作）；句意是新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。

pos.zh: 形容词：高效的；能干的；有产生力的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ency 构成，义为「效率」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「高效地」
由本词加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「低效的」
由 inefficient 加 -ency 构成，义为「低效」

senses.title: Working without waste
senses.definition: working well and completely, with little waste of time, energy or materials
senses.definitionCN: 做事又好又完整，很少浪费时间、精力或材料
senses.example: The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。
senses.why: Efficient is the Latin efficiens, doing or accomplishing: a thing that gets the work done without spending more than it must.
senses.whyCN: efficient 是拉丁语 efficiens，意为「正在做成的」：把活干成，却不比必须的多花一分。

senses.title: Organized and capable
senses.definition: of a person, organized and able to do a job well and quickly
senses.definitionCN: 指人时，有条理、能把事情做好做快
senses.example: She is an efficient manager who never wastes a meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个能干的经理，从不开没有结果的会。
senses.why: A person who finishes work without waste shows the same power to accomplish, so the adjective moves from machines to people.
senses.whyCN: 不浪费却把活完成的人，显露的是同一种「做成」的力量，于是这个形容词从机器移到了人身上。

senses.title: Having the power to produce an effect
senses.definition: having the power to bring about a result, as in the technical phrase efficient cause
senses.definitionCN: 具有产生结果的力量，用于「动力因」这一术语
senses.example: In philosophy, an efficient cause is what brings something about.
senses.exampleCN: 在哲学里，动力因就是使某物产生的东西。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply producing: an efficient cause is the doer that makes the effect exist.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「产生」：动力因是让结果存在起来的那个施行者。

intro.en: Efficient comes from Latin efficiens, the present participle of efficere, to accomplish, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: efficient 来自拉丁语 efficiens，即 efficere（完成）的现在分词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make and supplied the base of the verb.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，提供这个动词的词基。

items.en: Ex- out plus facere formed efficere, to work out or accomplish.
items.cn: 表示「出」的 ex- 加 facere 构成 efficere，意为「做出、完成」。

items.en: The participle efficiens described something as accomplishing or producing.
items.cn: 分词 efficiens 描述某物正在完成或正在产生。

items.en: French passed the adjective on with the sense of producing a result.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词传下来，意思是「能产生结果的」。

items.en: Industry added the everyday sense of working without waste of time or fuel.
items.cn: 工业又加入了日常义：不浪费时间或燃料地把活干好。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the efficiency family; the near-meaning group separates effective, productive and economical.
note.cn: 形近组收 efficiency 词族；近义组区分 effective、productive 与 economical。

entries.definition: The quality of working without waste, or the output-to-input ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「效率」，即不浪费的品质或产出投入之比。

entries.definition: In a manner that wastes little time or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「高效地」，很少浪费时间或精力。

entries.definition: The power to reach the intended result, with no claim about waste.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有效性」，只管结果达没达到，不管浪不浪费。

entries.definition: Producing the result wanted; it asks whether the aim is reached, not what it cost.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有效的」，只问目标是否达到，不问成本。

entries.definition: Producing a good amount of work or goods; it stresses output.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多产的」，强调产出量。

entries.definition: Saving money or resources; it stresses the cost spared.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「节约的」，强调省下的花费。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line that leaves no scrap on the floor, then move to a tidy manager and to a cause that makes things happen.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一条地上没有剩料的流水线出发，再走到干练的经理与「让事情发生」的原因。

normal.en: Efficient means the same work with less fuel, less time and less scrap.
normal.cn: efficient 就是用更少的燃料、时间和废料完成同样的活。

normal.en: An efficient manager ends the meeting when the decision is made.
normal.cn: 能干的经理在决定做出时就结束会议。

normal.en: Efficient and effective are cousins: one saves, the other arrives.
normal.cn: efficient 与 effective 是表亲：一个讲省，一个讲结果到了。

normal.en: The old philosophical sense is plain: efficient cause means the doer.
normal.cn: 古老的哲学义很直白：efficient cause 就是那个施行者。

normal.en: Efficiency is the noun, efficiently the adverb, inefficient the opposite.
normal.cn: efficiency 是名词，efficiently 是副词，inefficient 是反义。

abstract.en: Picture a factory line with parts going in and products coming out.
abstract.cn: 想象一条工厂流水线，零件进去，成品出来。

abstract.en: Look at the floor: nothing usable is left lying there.
abstract.cn: 再看地面：没有还能用的东西被丢在那里。

abstract.en: Efficient is that picture of full output and empty waste.
abstract.cn: efficient 就是「产出满、废料空」的那幅图。

examples.en: The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
examples.cn: 新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。

examples.en: She is an efficient manager who never wastes a meeting.
examples.cn: 她是个能干的经理，从不开没有结果的会。

examples.en: In philosophy, an efficient cause is what brings something about.
examples.cn: 在哲学里，动力因就是使某物产生的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊菲申特」——同一条流水线，地上没有剩料

root: 拉丁语 facere「做」加 ex-「出」构成 efficere「完成」，其现在分词 efficiens 指「正在做成的」，经法语 efficient 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of efficient: working without waste, a person who is organized and capable, and the technical sense of producing an effect.
sensesIntro.cn: efficient 的三个义项：不浪费地把活干好、人干练有条理，以及「能产生结果」的术语义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a production line with parts going in, products coming out, and no scrap on the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条流水线，零件进去，成品出来，地上没有剩料。

branches.en: THE SAVING: the same work is done with less fuel and less scrap.
branches.cn: 节省线：同样的活，用更少的燃料与废料完成。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a worker whose desk and schedule leave no waste.
branches.cn: 人物线：桌面与日程都不留浪费的工作者。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: the doer that makes the result exist.
branches.cn: 原因线：让结果存在起来的那个施行者。

branches.en: THE POWER: both senses are about producing, one with economy and one in philosophy.
branches.cn: 力量线：两个义项都关乎「产生」，一个讲节省，一个讲哲学。

branches.en: THE HABIT: a person can be as efficient as a well-tuned machine.
branches.cn: 习惯线：人可以像调好的机器一样高效。

intro.en: Efficient carries the Latin participle ending -ens; English adds -ency, -ly and the negative prefix in-.
intro.cn: efficient 带着拉丁语分词词尾 -ens；英语再加 -ency、-ly 与否定前缀 in-。

latinIntro.en: Latin efficere and efficiens are recorded, so only the Indo-European base of facere is reconstructed.

definition_zh: 努力；费力；尝试；成果；（集体的）行动
definition_en: the use of physical or mental energy, an attempt, a piece of work judged by its quality, or an organized campaign
core_image: 一根绳子被拉到最紧，掌心留下绳纹
scene: 他连着拉了十次绳子，帆才终于升到顶。It took a great effort to raise the sail.
sceneCN: 这里 effort 是「力气、努力」（第 1 个义项：身体或精神上的用力）；句意是升起船帆费了很大力气。

pos.zh: 名词：努力；费力；尝试；成果；集体行动

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -less 构成，义为「毫不费力的」
由 effortless 加 -ly 构成，义为「毫不费力地」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「费力的」

senses.title: Physical or mental exertion
senses.definition: the use of energy, strength or thought in order to do something
senses.definitionCN: 为了做成某事而付出的精力、力气或心思
senses.example: It took a great effort to raise the sail.
senses.exampleCN: 升起船帆费了很大力气。
senses.why: Effort comes from a French verb meaning to force or strengthen: it is strength put out on purpose.
senses.whyCN: effort 来自一个意为「用力、使强壮」的法语动词：它是有意拿出来的力气。

senses.title: An attempt
senses.definition: an act of trying to do something, especially when success is not certain
senses.definitionCN: 试图做成某事的行动，尤指结果并不确定时
senses.example: He made one last effort to reach the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 他拼尽最后一番努力想游到岸边。
senses.why: A burst of strength aimed at a goal is also a try, so effort names the attempt itself.
senses.whyCN: 朝目标爆发的一股力气也是一次尝试，于是 effort 也指尝试本身。

senses.title: A piece of work judged by its quality
senses.definition: a particular attempt or achievement, often judged as good or poor
senses.definitionCN: 某一次尝试或成果，常被评价为好或差
senses.example: Her first novel was a fine effort.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说是部不错的作品。
senses.why: What has been produced by exerted strength can stand as the work itself, so the effort is the result.
senses.whyCN: 用力之后产出的东西可以当作作品本身，于是这份努力就成了成果。

senses.title: An organized campaign
senses.definition: a coordinated attempt by a group of people, often for aid, rescue or change
senses.definitionCN: 一群人协调一致的行动，常指援助、救援或推动改变
senses.example: The relief effort reached the village by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 救援行动在中午前抵达了村子。
senses.why: Many people putting out strength together form one shared effort, so the word can name a whole campaign.
senses.whyCN: 许多人一起把力气拿出来，汇成一份共同的努力，于是这个词可以指整场行动。

intro.en: Effort comes from Old French esforz, from the verb esforcier, to force or strengthen, and goes back to Latin fortis, strong.
intro.cn: effort 来自古法语 esforz，源自动词 esforcier（用力、使强壮），更早追溯到拉丁语 fortis（强壮的）。

items.en: Fortis meant strong, and it is the root of force and effort alike.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮的」，是 force 与 effort 共同的根。

items.en: Fortia named strength or force, the quality that can be put out.
items.cn: fortia 指力量或强力，即可以被拿出来的那种品质。

items.en: The verb meant to force, strengthen or exert oneself.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「使劲、加强、竭力」。

items.en: The noun named an exertion, a striving or a feat of strength.
items.cn: 名词指一次用力、一番拼搏或一场力量之举。

items.en: English borrowed it for the act of trying hard and later for the attempt itself.
items.cn: 英语借入后表示「努力去做」，后来又指尝试本身。

items.en: The sense of a shared campaign grew from many people exerting themselves together.
items.cn: 「共同行动」一义由许多人一起用力的情形发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on effort; the near-meaning group separates attempt, exertion and endeavor.
note.cn: 形近组收由 effort 构成的词；近义组区分 attempt、exertion 与 endeavor。

entries.definition: Needing no effort; formed from effort with -less.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毫不费力的」，由 effort 加 -less 构成。

entries.definition: In a way that shows no effort; effortless plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「毫不费力地」，由 effortless 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Requiring noticeable effort; effort plus -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「费力的」，由 effort 加 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: An act of trying; it names the try more than the strength spent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「尝试」，更强调「试」而不是花掉多少力气。

entries.definition: Hard physical or mental work; it stresses the strain itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「费力、劳累」，强调承受的紧张。

entries.definition: A serious attempt or undertaking; more formal and more purposeful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「努力、事业」，更正式、更有目标感。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow one rope pulled tight, then a last try, then a finished piece and a shared rescue.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着一根拉紧的绳子，再走到最后一次尝试、一件成品与一场共同救援。

normal.en: Effort is strength put out on purpose.
normal.cn: effort 就是有意拿出来的力气。

normal.en: The rope leaves its mark on the palm: that mark is effort.
normal.cn: 绳子在掌心留下纹路：那道纹就是 effort。

normal.en: One last pull can be both an effort and an attempt.
normal.cn: 最后一把拉，既是一份力气，也是一次尝试。

normal.en: A fine effort is a piece of work you judge, not a muscle you measure.
normal.cn: a fine effort 是你评价的作品，不是你测量的肌肉。

normal.en: A relief effort is many people's strength gathered into one campaign.
normal.cn: relief effort 是许多人的力气汇成一场行动。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled until it hums.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子被拉到发出嗡响。

abstract.en: The same pull can be a try, a finished work, or a village rescue.
abstract.cn: 同一次拉，可以是一次尝试、一件成品，或一场村庄救援。

abstract.en: Effort is what it costs to move something that does not move by itself.
abstract.cn: effort 就是推动一个自己不会动的东西所要付出的代价。

examples.en: It took a great effort to raise the sail.
examples.cn: 升起船帆费了很大力气。

examples.en: He made one last effort to reach the shore.
examples.cn: 他拼尽最后一番努力想游到岸边。

examples.en: The relief effort reached the village by noon.
examples.cn: 救援行动在中午前抵达了村子。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of effort: exertion, an attempt, a piece of work judged by quality, and an organized campaign.
sensesIntro.cn: effort 的四个义项：用力、尝试、被评价的成果，以及有组织的集体行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope pulled tight, leaving its mark on the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子被拉到最紧，掌心留下绳纹。

branches.en: THE STRAIN: energy of body or mind put into the work.
branches.cn: 用力线：身体或心思被投进工作里的能量。

branches.en: THE TRY: the same burst of strength aimed at a goal.
branches.cn: 尝试线：同一股力气朝着目标使出去。

branches.en: THE WORK: what the strength produced, judged as good or poor.
branches.cn: 成果线：力气产出的东西，被评好或评差。

branches.en: THE CAMPAIGN: many people's strength gathered into one action.
branches.cn: 行动线：许多人的力气汇成一次行动。

branches.en: ONE PULL: every attempt begins with strength deliberately spent.
branches.cn: 同一把拉：每次尝试都从有意花掉的力气开始。

intro.en: Effort is a French noun in -t built on a verb of forcing; English adds -less, -ful and -ly.
intro.cn: effort 是以 -t 收尾的法语名词，建立在表示「使劲」的动词上；英语再加 -less、-ful 与 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis and fortia are recorded; the French verb and noun are attested, so no layer here is reconstructed except the oldest root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 与 fortia 均有记录，法语动词与名词也有书证，因此除最古老词根外没有重构层次。

items.example: It is the deepest recorded root.
items.exampleCN: 它是有记录的最深词根。

items.example: It names strength as a thing.
items.exampleCN: 它把力量作为一个事物来命名。

scene: 清晨的锅里，水一开，壳里的东西很快凝成白色。She cracked an egg into the boiling water.

pos.zh: 名词：蛋；卵；卵细胞
动词：怂恿；鼓动

derivatives.zh: 由 egg 与 shell 复合，义为「蛋壳」
由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「有蛋味的；像蛋的」

senses.title: The body laid by a female bird
senses.definition: the oval object with a shell that a female bird lays, eaten as food or hatched into a chick
senses.definitionCN: 雌鸟产下的带壳椭圆体，可作食物，也可孵出小鸟
senses.example: She cracked an egg into the boiling water.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一只蛋磕进沸水里。
senses.why: The noun came from Old Norse egg, the everyday word for the shelled body a bird lays.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自古诺尔斯语 egg，就是鸟产下的那个带壳物体的日常说法。

senses.title: A female reproductive cell
senses.definition: the ovum, the cell produced by a female that joins with a sperm in reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 雌性产生、在生殖中与精子结合的细胞，即卵细胞
senses.example: Each egg carries half of the genetic material.
senses.exampleCN: 每个卵细胞携带一半的遗传物质。
senses.why: The bird's egg is one cell writ large, so biology uses the same word for the ovum.
senses.whyCN: 鸟蛋就是一个被放大的细胞，因此生物学用同一个词指卵细胞。

senses.title: To urge someone on
senses.definition: to encourage someone to do something, often something risky or foolish
senses.definitionCN: 鼓励某人去做某事，常指冒险或不明智的事
senses.example: His friends egged him on to jump.
senses.exampleCN: 他的朋友们怂恿他跳下去。
senses.why: This verb is a different word: Old English eggian meant to incite, and it merely shares the spelling of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是另一个词：古英语 eggian 意为「煽动」，只是与名词拼写相同。

intro.en: The noun egg came from Old Norse, while the verb egg on came separately from Old English eggian; the two are unrelated despite the shared spelling.
intro.cn: 名词 egg 来自古诺尔斯语，动词 egg on 则另出自古英语 eggian；两者拼写相同，来源却无关。

items.en: Old Norse egg named the shelled body laid by a bird, and it replaced the older English word.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 egg 指鸟产下的带壳之物，并取代了英语原有的说法。

items.en: Middle English kept the Norse word for the food and the hatchable body.
items.cn: 中古英语保留这个诺尔斯语词，指食物与可孵化的卵。

items.en: A separate verb eggian meant to incite or provoke, and it survives only in egg on.
items.cn: 另一个动词 eggian 意为「煽动、挑动」，只存活在 egg on 这一短语里。

items.en: The noun widened from the bird's egg to the ovum and to egg as food.
items.cn: 名词从鸟蛋扩展到卵细胞，也固定为食物意义上的蛋。

items.en: The homographs now sit in one dictionary entry, though their histories never met.
items.cn: 这两个同形词如今列在同一词条里，但它们的历史从未相遇。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derived forms of egg; the near-meaning group separates ovum, spawn and roe.
note.cn: 形近组收 egg 的复合词与派生形式；近义组区分 ovum、spawn 与 roe。

entries.definition: The hard outer shell of an egg.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蛋壳」，由 egg 与 shell 复合。

entries.definition: Sounding or tasting of egg.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有蛋味的」，由 egg 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: Made without egg.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不含蛋的」，由 egg 加 -less 构成。

entries.definition: The scientific word for a female reproductive cell.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「卵细胞」，是科学术语。

entries.definition: The eggs of fish or frogs laid in water in a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鱼或蛙产在水中的卵块」。

entries.definition: Fish eggs, especially when eaten as food.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鱼卵」，尤指作为食物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one shell in a pan, then move to a cell and to a voice urging someone to jump.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从锅里的一只蛋壳出发，再走到一个细胞，以及一个鼓动别人跳下去的声音。

normal.en: An egg is a shell with a cell inside, and both meanings grow from that.
normal.cn: egg 是壳里裹着一个细胞，两个义项都从这里长出来。

normal.en: Crack it into boiling water and the white sets at once.
normal.cn: 磕进沸水里，蛋白立刻凝住。

normal.en: In biology the same word shrinks to the single cell.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，同一个词缩小成那一个细胞。

normal.en: Egg on has nothing to do with the noun: it is an old verb for inciting.
normal.cn: egg on 与名词无关：它是一个表示「煽动」的古动词。

normal.en: Eggshell, eggy and eggless all keep the noun's plain shape.
normal.cn: eggshell、eggy、eggless 都保留名词的朴素词形。

abstract.en: Picture one oval shape sitting in three different places.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个椭圆形状出现在三个不同地方。

abstract.en: In a pan it is breakfast, under a microscope it is a cell, in a shout it is a dare.
abstract.cn: 在锅里是早餐，在显微镜下是细胞，在一声喊里是挑动。

abstract.en: Egg is one shape with two histories that only share a spelling.
abstract.cn: egg 是一个形状带着两段历史，而这两段只共用拼写。

examples.en: She cracked an egg into the boiling water.
examples.cn: 她把一只蛋磕进沸水里。

examples.en: Birds sit on their eggs until they hatch.
examples.cn: 鸟坐在蛋上直到它们孵出。

examples.en: His friends egged him on to jump.
examples.cn: 他的朋友们怂恿他跳下去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埃格」——一只蛋磕进沸水，蛋白立刻凝成白色

root: 名词 egg 借自古诺尔斯语，指鸟产的带壳卵；动词 egg on 另出自古英语 eggian「煽动」，二者同形而异源。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of egg: the shelled body laid by a bird, the female reproductive cell, and the unrelated verb meaning to urge on.
sensesIntro.cn: egg 的三个义项：鸟产下的带壳卵、雌性生殖细胞，以及同形异源、表示「怂恿」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an egg cracked into boiling water, its white setting at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只蛋磕进沸水，蛋白立刻凝成白色。

branches.en: THE FOOD: the shelled body a bird lays and people cook.
branches.cn: 食物线：鸟产下、人们烹食的带壳卵。

branches.en: THE CELL: the same shape shrunk to a single ovum.
branches.cn: 细胞线：同一形状缩小成一个卵细胞。

branches.en: THE SHOUT: a separate old verb that only shares the spelling.
branches.cn: 喊声线：另一个古动词，只共用拼写。

branches.en: THE NEST: the laid egg and the ovum are the same biology at two scales.
branches.cn: 巢线：产下的蛋与卵细胞是同一套生理的两个尺度。

branches.en: THE SPLIT: one dictionary entry, two unrelated histories.
branches.cn: 分裂线：一个词条，两段无关的历史。

intro.en: Egg is a short native-looking noun of Norse origin; English builds compounds and a few suffixes on it.
intro.cn: egg 是源自诺尔斯语、看起来像本土词的短名词；英语在它上面构成复合词与少量派生词。

latinIntro.en: Neither the Norse noun nor the Old English verb is Latin, so no Latin entry is claimed here; only the spelling is shared.
latinIntro.cn: 诺尔斯语名词与古英语动词都不是拉丁语，因此这里不列拉丁语条目；两者只共用拼写。

items.meaning: the shelled body laid by a bird
items.example: It is the source of the noun.

items.exampleCN: 它存活在 egg on 中。

definition_zh: 两者中任一的；两者各一的；也（用于否定）；或者
definition_en: one or the other of two, each of the two, also in a negative sentence, or used in either or
core_image: 两条并排的路，站在岔口的人只能挑一条
scene: 路口只分出两条路，她把水壶检查了两遍才动身。Either road will take you to the mill.
sceneCN: 这里 either 是「两者中任一的」（第 1 个义项：两条路里的任何一条）；句意是两条路中哪一条都能到磨坊。

pos.zh: 限定词：两者中任一的；两者各一的
代词：两者之一
副词：也（用于否定句）
连词：either... or 或者……或者

collocations.zh: 不管哪种方式；两种都行

forms.label: 无屈折变化（限定词、代词、副词、连词）

derivatives.zh: 由本词与 or 复合，义为「非此即彼的；二选一的」
由本词的否定形式演变而来，义为「两者都不」

senses.title: One or the other of two
senses.definition: one or the other of two people or things, it does not matter which
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或物中的任何一个，不论哪一个
senses.example: Either road will take you to the mill.
senses.exampleCN: 两条路中哪一条都能到磨坊。
senses.why: Either began as the old word for each of two, and a free choice between two grew out of that.
senses.whyCN: either 最初是「两者各自」的古老说法，两者之间的自由选择就从这个意思长出来。

senses.title: Each of the two
senses.definition: each of the two, used after a singular noun to mean both sides
senses.definitionCN: 两者各自，用在单数名词后表示两边的意思
senses.example: The lane is lined with poplars on either side.
senses.exampleCN: 小路两边都种着白杨。
senses.why: The older sense of each survives in phrases like on either side, where both sides are meant.
senses.whyCN: 更古老的「各自」义保留在 on either side 这样的说法里，实际指的是两边。

senses.title: Also, in a negative sentence
senses.definition: used at the end of a negative statement to add another negative point
senses.definitionCN: 用于否定句末尾，再补充一个否定内容
senses.example: I have not finished, and my brother has not either.
senses.exampleCN: 我没做完，我弟弟也没做完。
senses.why: If not one of two is so, then not the other one either: the pronoun turns into a sentence-ending adverb.
senses.whyCN: 如果两者之一不是如此，那么另一个也不是：代词就这样变成了句末副词。

senses.title: Either or as a pair
senses.definition: used before two choices to show that one of them must be chosen
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个选项之前，表示必须从中选择一个
senses.example: Either you sign now or you lose the place.
senses.exampleCN: 你要么现在签字，要么就失去这个名额。
senses.why: The choice between two is stated as a pair, and either heads the first branch of the fork.
senses.whyCN: 两者之间的选择被摆成一对，either 站在岔路的第一条分支上。

intro.en: Either comes from Old English ǣgther, a contraction of ǣghwæther, each of two, from the root that also gives each.
intro.cn: either 来自古英语 ǣgther，是 ǣghwæther（两者各自）的缩合形式，其词根也生出 each。

items.en: The compound meant each of the two, built on a root meaning ever and which.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「两者各自」，建立在表示「每一个、哪一个」的词根上。

items.en: The contracted form kept the sense of each of two without exception.
items.cn: 缩合形式保留「两者中无一例外」的意思。

items.en: Further contraction produced ǣgther, the direct ancestor of either.
items.cn: 进一步缩合产生 ǣgther，即 either 的直系祖先。

items.en: Middle English weakened the first sound and settled the spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语弱化了第一个音，固定了拼写。

items.en: The sense widened from each of two to one or the other, and the adverb use grew from negatives.
items.cn: 词义从「两者各自」扩展到「两者之一」，副词用法则从否定句中长出。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the paired determiners; the near-meaning group separates any, both and neither.
note.cn: 形近组收成对的限定词；近义组区分 any、both 与 neither。

entries.definition: Not one and not the other of two, the negative partner of either.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「两者都不」，是 either 的否定搭档。

entries.definition: A substance once thought to fill all space, or a chemical solvent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「以太」或「乙醚」，拼写相近但来源不同。

entries.definition: Very keen to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「热切的」，与 either 仅部分拼写相似。

entries.definition: One or some of a larger set, not limited to two.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「任何」，范围大于两个。

entries.definition: The two together, not one of them.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「两者都」，是合起来而不是选一个。

entries.definition: Any one of a set that is not limited to two.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「无论哪一个」，不限于两个。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin at a fork with two roads, then show how the same word becomes both, also, and a paired choice.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从有两条路的岔口出发，再看同一个词如何变成「两边」「也不」与成对的选择。

normal.en: Either lives at a fork: exactly two roads, and you take one.
normal.cn: either 住在岔口：正好两条路，你走其中一条。

normal.en: On either side means on both sides, the older sense of each.
normal.cn: on either side 指两边，是「各自」这个更古老的意思。

normal.en: In a negative sentence, either moves to the end and means too.
normal.cn: 在否定句里，either 跑到句末，意思是「也」。

normal.en: Either you stay or you go: the fork is spoken as a pair.
normal.cn: 要么留、要么走：岔口被说成了一对。

normal.en: Add n and you get neither, the fork with no road taken.
normal.cn: 前面加 n 就成了 neither，即两条路都不走。

abstract.en: Picture a stone signpost with two arms pointing different ways.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石制路牌，两条手臂指向不同方向。

abstract.en: The same post can name one road, both roads, or a refusal of both.
abstract.cn: 同一块路牌可以说一条路、两条路，或两条都不走。

abstract.en: Either is a choice held open at the moment before it is made.
abstract.cn: either 就是选择做出之前那个仍然敞开的状态。

examples.en: Either road will take you to the mill.
examples.cn: 两条路中哪一条都能到磨坊。

examples.en: The lane is lined with poplars on either side.
examples.cn: 小路两边都种着白杨。

examples.en: I have not finished, and my brother has not either.
examples.cn: 我没做完，我弟弟也没做完。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挨则」——岔口两条路，挨着挑哪条都行

root: 古英语 ǣgther 是 ǣghwæther「两者各自」的缩合形式，词根同时生出 each；词义由「各自」扩展为「两者之一」，再由否定句生出「也」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of either: one of two, each of the two, also in negatives, and the paired choice either or.
sensesIntro.cn: either 的四个义项：两者之一、两者各自、否定句中的「也」，以及 either or 的成对选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fork with exactly two roads and a traveller who must pick one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个只有两条路的岔口，行人必须挑一条。

branches.en: THE CHOICE: one road, it does not matter which.
branches.cn: 选择线：走一条，不限哪条。

branches.en: THE PAIR: each of the two, as in on either side.
branches.cn: 成对线：两者各自，如 on either side。

branches.en: THE NEGATIVE: not one, and not the other either.
branches.cn: 否定线：一个不是，另一个也不是。

branches.en: THE FORK SPOKEN ALOUD: either this or that.
branches.cn: 出声的岔口：或者这个，或者那个。

branches.en: THE TWO ENDS: choosing one and naming both grow from the same pair.
branches.cn: 两端线：选一个与指两者，都从同一对里长出。

intro.en: Either is a worn-down Old English compound rather than a prefixed Latin word; its parts are no longer separable.
intro.cn: either 是磨蚀的古英语复合词，而非拉丁语加前缀的词；它的构件今天已不可再分。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin layer; the Indo-European root behind the old compound is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语，没有拉丁语层次；古老复合词背后的印欧词根属于重构。

It is a shortened form of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个复合词的缩短形式。

items.example: It is the direct source form.

items.meaning: every one of two or more
items.example: It shares the same old root.
items.exampleCN: 它与本词共用同一个古老词根。

items.example: It is either with a negative first element.
items.exampleCN: 它是 either 前加否定成分。
它由 either 与 or 复合。

items.example: It survives inside the old pair words.
items.exampleCN: 它残留在这一对古词之中。
它标记这种二选一的对比。

definition_zh: 年长的；上了年纪的；老年人
definition_en: rather old, used politely of people past middle age, or the group of old people as a whole
core_image: 公园长椅上，一位老人把围巾又拢紧了些
scene: 长椅上那位老人扶着扶手才站起来，动作很慢。An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
sceneCN: 这里 elderly 是「年长的」（第 1 个义项：客气地指已过中年、年纪较大的人）；句意是一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。

pos.zh: 形容词：年长的；上了年纪的（较礼貌）
名词：the elderly 老年人（集合）

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ly 得到，义为「年长的；长辈」
由 elderly 加 -ness 构成，义为「年长；老年」

senses.title: Rather old, said politely
senses.definition: past middle age and getting old, used as a polite word instead of old
senses.definitionCN: 已过中年、渐渐年老，用作 old 的客气说法
senses.example: An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。
senses.why: Elderly is elder plus -ly, and elder is the comparative of old: it says older, gently, without the bluntness of old.
senses.whyCN: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly，而 elder 是 old 的比较级：它温和地说「更年长」，没有 old 那么直白。

senses.title: Old people as a group
senses.definition: with the, old people considered as a group in society
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指社会中作为一个群体的老年人
senses.example: The clinic offers free transport for the elderly.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为老年人提供免费接送。
senses.why: An adjective with the can name a whole class, so the elderly means all who answer to that description.
senses.whyCN: 形容词加 the 可以指整个类别，所以 the elderly 就是所有符合这个描述的人。

senses.title: Old and worn, said with a smile
senses.definition: used humorously of things that are old and worn out
senses.definitionCN: 戏谑地用于年久失修、老旧的物件
senses.example: My elderly laptop takes ten minutes to start.
senses.exampleCN: 我那台老掉牙的笔记本要十分钟才启动。
senses.why: The polite word for old people is transferred to machines, and the politeness itself becomes the joke.
senses.whyCN: 这个对人客气的词被挪到机器上，那份客气本身就成了笑话。

intro.en: Elderly is elder plus -ly; elder is the old comparative of old, from Old English eldra, and still carries the sense of seniority.
intro.cn: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly；elder 是 old 的古老比较级，来自古英语 eldra，至今仍带「辈分较长」的意味。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective meant old or grown up.
items.cn: 重构形容词意为「年老的、长成的」。

items.en: Eldra was the comparative of eald, old, and meant older.
items.cn: eldra 是 eald（老）的比较级，意为「更年长的」。

items.en: Elder kept the sense of senior in age or rank, especially within a family.
items.cn: elder 保留年龄或辈分较长的意思，尤用于家族内部。

items.en: The ending -ly softened the adjective into a polite description of age.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把这个形容词软化，成为对年龄的客气描述。

items.en: The elderly settled as a collective name, and the word spread jokingly to worn objects.
items.cn: the elderly 固定为集合称谓，这个词又戏谑地扩展到破旧物件上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elder family; the near-meaning group separates old, senior and aged by tone.
note.cn: 形近组收 elder 词族；近义组按语气区分 old、senior 与 aged。

entries.definition: Older, especially of a relative or a person of authority in a community.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼名词，义为「年长的；长辈」，是本词的词基。

entries.definition: The oldest of a group, usually of brothers or sisters.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最年长的」，多指兄弟姐妹中的老大。

entries.definition: Having lived a long time; plainer and blunter than elderly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「老的」，比 elderly 更直白。

entries.definition: Older or higher in rank, often used in official contexts such as senior citizens.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年长的、资深的」，常用于 senior citizens 等正式说法。

entries.definition: Very old; it can sound more formal or more pointed than elderly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年迈的」，比 elderly 更正式或更强调。

entries.definition: Growing old, said of a process rather than a person's state.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「老龄化的」，描述过程而非人的状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from elder as the gentle comparative of old, then follow the word into a group name and a joke about machines.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从 elder 这个温和的比较级出发，再走到群体称谓与关于机器的玩笑。

normal.en: Elderly is elder plus -ly: the polite way of saying older.
normal.cn: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly：说「更年长」时的客气说法。

normal.en: Old can sting; elderly steps back and leaves room.
normal.cn: old 可能刺人；elderly 往后退半步，留出余地。

normal.en: The elderly are not one person but a whole group.
normal.cn: the elderly 不是一个人，而是一整群人。

normal.en: My elderly laptop is a joke: the politeness is the point.
normal.cn: my elderly laptop 是个玩笑：那份客气本身就是笑点。

normal.en: Elderly usually starts around retirement age, old goes further.
normal.cn: elderly 大约从退休年龄起算，old 还要再往后。

abstract.en: Picture a slow rise from a park bench, hands on the armrest.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人双手扶着扶手，从公园长椅上慢慢起身。

abstract.en: The same politeness can cover a person, a group, or a tired machine.
abstract.cn: 同一份客气可以覆盖一个人、一群人，或一台疲惫的机器。

abstract.en: Elderly is old with a hand held out.
abstract.cn: elderly 就是伸出手扶一把的 old。

examples.en: An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
examples.cn: 一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。

examples.en: The clinic offers free transport for the elderly.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为老年人提供免费接送。

examples.en: My elderly laptop takes ten minutes to start.
examples.cn: 我那台老掉牙的笔记本要十分钟才启动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埃尔德利」——老人扶着扶手，才慢慢站起来

root: elderly 由 elder 加 -ly 构成；elder 是 old 的古老比较级（古英语 eldra），故本词字面即「更年长的」，语气比 old 委婉。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elderly: politely old, old people as a group, and humorously worn out.
sensesIntro.cn: elderly 的三个义项：客气地说年长、作为群体的老年人，以及戏称物件老旧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old person rising slowly from a bench, one hand on the armrest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位老人扶着扶手，从长椅上慢慢起身。

branches.en: THE PERSON: past middle age, described politely.
branches.cn: 人物线：已过中年，用客气的方式描述。

branches.en: THE CLASS: with the, all such people together.
branches.cn: 群体线：加 the 指所有这样的人。

branches.en: THE JOKE: the same politeness spent on a tired laptop.
branches.cn: 玩笑线：同一份客气用在一台疲惫的笔记本上。

branches.en: THE TONE: the word's gentleness is what joins person and group.
branches.cn: 语气线：这个词的温和把个人与群体连在一起。

branches.en: THE TRANSFER: respect for age becomes mock respect for age in objects.
branches.cn: 转移线：对年岁的敬重变成对物件年岁的假敬重。

intro.en: Elderly is a native English adjective built on the old comparative elder with the ending -ly.
intro.cn: elderly 是英语本土形容词，由古老比较级 elder 加词尾 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic and recorded in Old English, so no Latin entry is claimed here.
latinIntro.cn: 两个构件都属于日耳曼语且在古英语中有记录，因此这里不列拉丁语条目。

items.example: It is the positive form behind elder.
items.exampleCN: 它是 elder 背后的原级。

items.example: It is the source of elder.
It is the base of elderly.

definition_zh: 选举；推选；选择决定；当选而尚未就职的
definition_en: to choose someone by voting, to decide to do something, or describing someone chosen but not yet in office
core_image: 一只只手举起，票箱被封上，名字被念出来
scene: 会场里一只手接一只手举起，票数很快过半。The members elected a new chair by a clear majority.
sceneCN: 这里 elect 是「选举」（第 1 个义项：通过投票选出某人）；句意是成员以明显多数选出了新主席。

pos.zh: 动词：选举；推选；选择做（某事）
形容词：当选而尚未就职的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「选举」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「选举的；选修的；选修课」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「选民；选举人」
由 elector 加 -al 构成，义为「选举的」

senses.title: To choose by voting
senses.definition: to choose a person for an office or position by voting
senses.definitionCN: 通过投票为某个职位选出某人
senses.example: The members elected a new chair by a clear majority.
senses.exampleCN: 成员以明显多数选出了新主席。
senses.why: Elect is Latin eligere, e- out plus legere to pick: the choice is picked out and then made public.
senses.whyCN: elect 是拉丁语 eligere，由 e-（出）加 legere（挑选）构成：这个选择被挑出来，然后公开。

senses.title: To decide to do something
senses.definition: to choose to do something, especially in formal or official language
senses.definitionCN: 选择去做某事，尤用于正式或官方语境
senses.example: The company elected to remain silent.
senses.exampleCN: 公司选择保持沉默。
senses.why: The same picking happens inside one head instead of a hall, so elect can mean simply to choose.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「挑选」发生在一个脑袋里而不是大厅里，所以 elect 也能只表示「选择」。

senses.title: Chosen but not yet in office
senses.definition: used after a title for someone who has been elected but has not yet taken up the post
senses.definitionCN: 用在头衔之后，指已经当选但尚未上任的人
senses.example: The president elect will be sworn in in January.
senses.exampleCN: 当选总统将于一月宣誓就职。
senses.why: The pick has been made but the office is still empty, so the adjective marks that gap in time.
senses.whyCN: 人选已经挑定，而职位还空着，于是这个形容词标记出这段时间空隙。

intro.en: Elect comes from Latin eligere, to pick out, from e- out plus legere, to choose or read, and reached English through the participle electus.
intro.cn: elect 来自拉丁语 eligere（挑出），由 e-（出）加 legere（挑选、读）构成，经分词 electus 进入英语。

items.en: Legere meant to gather, pick or read, and it also gave lecture and legend.
items.cn: legere 意为「收集、挑选、读」，也生出 lecture 与 legend。

items.en: E- out plus legere formed eligere, to pick out from among others.
items.cn: e-（出）加 legere 构成 eligere，意为「从众人中挑出来」。

items.en: The participle electus meant picked out, hence chosen.
items.cn: 分词 electus 意为「被挑出的」，因此是「被选中的」。

items.en: The noun named the act of picking out, the source of election.
items.cn: 名词指「挑选」这一动作，是 election 的来源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb for choosing a person to an office.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，指为某个职位选出人选。

items.en: The bare verb also took the milder sense of deciding, and the adjective use followed.
items.cn: 光杆动词又带上「决定」的温和义，形容词用法随后出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the election family; the near-meaning group separates choose, vote and appoint.
note.cn: 形近组收 election 词族；近义组区分 choose、vote 与 appoint。

entries.definition: The process of choosing someone by voting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选举」，由 elect 加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: Chosen by election, or a course a student may choose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼名词，义为「选举的；选修的；选修课」。

entries.definition: A person who has the right to vote in an election.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选民」，由 elect 加 -or 构成。

entries.definition: To pick one thing or person from several; the plain general verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「选择」，最普通的上位词。

entries.definition: To record a formal choice; it names the act inside an election.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投票」，指选举中的那个动作。

entries.definition: To give someone a job or post by decision rather than by vote.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「任命」，由决定而非投票产生。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hall of raised hands, then narrow to one private decision and one gap before taking office.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从举手的大厅出发，再缩到一个人的私下决定，以及上任前的那段空缺。

normal.en: Elect is e- out plus legere pick: to pick someone out.
normal.cn: elect 是 e-（出）加 legere（挑）：把某人挑出来。

normal.en: A hall of raised hands makes a vote into an election.
normal.cn: 一片举起的手把投票变成一场选举。

normal.en: A board can elect to stay silent: no votes, just a choice.
normal.cn: 董事会可以 elect to 保持沉默：没有投票，只有选择。

normal.en: President elect means chosen but not yet sworn in.
normal.cn: president elect 指已经选出、尚未宣誓就职。

normal.en: The same root gives lecture: picking words out of a page.
normal.cn: 同一个词根也生出 lecture：从书页上把词挑出来读。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a room full of hands.
abstract.cn: 想象满屋子的手，其中一只举了起来。

abstract.en: The same picking can be public or private, and it can leave a name standing alone.
abstract.cn: 同一种挑选可以是公开的或私下的，也可以让一个名字单独立着。

abstract.en: Elect means someone was taken out of the many on purpose.
abstract.cn: elect 意味着有人被有意地从众多中拿了出来。

examples.en: The members elected a new chair by a clear majority.
examples.cn: 成员以明显多数选出了新主席。

examples.en: The company elected to remain silent.
examples.cn: 公司选择保持沉默。

examples.en: The president elect will be sworn in in January.
examples.cn: 当选总统将于一月宣誓就职。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊莱克特」——满场举手，票箱一开名字就被挑出来

root: 拉丁语 legere「挑选、读」加前缀 e-「出」构成 eligere「挑出」，分词 electus 即「被选中的」，英语借入为「选举」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elect: choosing by vote, deciding to do something, and the adjective for someone chosen but not yet in office.
sensesIntro.cn: elect 的三个义项：投票选出、决定去做，以及「当选尚未就职」的形容词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forest of raised hands and one name read out of the box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片举起的手，一个名字从票箱里被念出。

branches.en: THE VOTE: the many choose one for an office.
branches.cn: 投票线：众人为职位选出一人。

branches.en: THE DECISION: the picking happens inside one mind.
branches.cn: 决定线：挑选发生在一个人心里。

branches.en: THE GAP: chosen already, in office not yet.
branches.cn: 空档线：已经选出，尚未上任。

branches.en: ONE GESTURE: public voting and private choosing are the same picking out.
branches.cn: 同一动作：公开投票与私下选择都是同一种挑出。

branches.en: THE WAIT: the vote ends, the title waits.
branches.cn: 等待线：投票结束，头衔还在等。

intro.en: Elect is e- plus the Latin picking verb; English adds -ion, -ive, -or and -al to build the family.
intro.cn: elect 是 e- 加拉丁语「挑选」动词；英语再加 -ion、-ive、-or 与 -al 构成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere, eligere and electus are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 legere、eligere 与 electus 均有记录，只有更深的印欧词根属于重构。

items.exampleCN: 它与 legere 构成 eligere。

items.example: It is the direct source verb.
It is the source of the English verb.

definition_zh: 选举；当选；选择（正式）
definition_en: the process of choosing someone by voting, the fact of being chosen, or a formal act of choosing
core_image: 投票站门口贴着一张名单，纸角被风吹起
scene: 晚上十点投票站关门，计票机随即开始运转。The election result came before midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 election 是「选举」（第 1 个义项：通过投票选出人的整个过程）；句意是选举结果在午夜前出来了。

pos.zh: 名词：选举；当选；（正式）选择

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ion 得到，义为「选举」
由 elector 加 -al 构成，义为「选举的」
由 elector 加 -ate 构成，义为「全体选民」
由本词加 -eer 构成，义为「进行竞选活动」

senses.title: The process of voting someone in
senses.definition: the organized process in which people vote to choose someone for an office
senses.definitionCN: 人们投票为某个职位选出人选的整套组织过程
senses.example: The election result came before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 选举结果在午夜前出来了。
senses.why: Election is the noun of eligere, to pick out: the whole machinery exists for one act of picking.
senses.whyCN: election 是 eligere（挑出）的名词：整套机器只为一次「挑出」而存在。

senses.title: The fact of being chosen
senses.definition: the state or event of being chosen for a post, seen from the winner's side
senses.definitionCN: 从当选者角度看，被选上某个职位这一事实
senses.example: Her election to the board surprised no one.
senses.exampleCN: 她当选董事，没人感到意外。
senses.why: The same picking seen from inside the winner becomes a personal event rather than a public process.
senses.whyCN: 同一次挑选若从当选者内部看，就成了个人事件，而不是公共过程。

senses.title: A formal act of choosing
senses.definition: a deliberate choice between options, used in formal or religious language
senses.definitionCN: 在选项之间作出的慎重选择，用于正式或宗教语境
senses.example: He made a deliberate election to stay silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他有意选择了保持沉默。
senses.why: Before it meant voting, the word simply named a choice; that older sense survives in formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「投票」之前，这个词只指一次选择；这个更古老的意思仍活在正式文章里。

intro.en: Election comes from Latin electio, the noun of eligere, to pick out, formed from e- out and legere, to choose.
intro.cn: election 来自拉丁语 electio，即 eligere（挑出）的名词，由 e-（出）与 legere（挑选）构成。

items.en: Legere meant to gather or pick, and it also gave lecture and legend.
items.cn: legere 意为「收集、挑选」，也生出 lecture 与 legend。

items.en: E- out plus legere formed the verb to pick out from among others.
items.cn: e-（出）加 legere 构成「从众人中挑出」的动词。

items.en: Electio named the act of picking out, at first any choice at all.
items.cn: electio 指「挑出」的动作，最初泛指任何选择。

items.en: French narrowed the noun toward choosing a person for an office.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词窄化为「为职位选人」。

items.en: English used it for both the choice and the gathering that makes it.
items.cn: 英语既用它指选择本身，也指做出选择的那场集会。

items.en: The voting sense dominates, while the plain sense of choice survives in formal style.
items.cn: 投票义占了主导，而朴素的「选择」义仍留在正式文体中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elect family; the near-meaning group separates vote, ballot and referendum.
note.cn: 形近组收 elect 词族；近义组区分 vote、ballot 与 referendum。

entries.definition: To choose someone for an office by voting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「选举」，是本词的动词词基。

entries.definition: Filled by election, or a course freely chosen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼名词，义为「选举产生的；选修的；选修课」。

entries.definition: All the people entitled to vote in an election.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「全体选民」。

entries.definition: To work actively for a candidate or party in a campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「进行竞选活动」。

entries.definition: A single formal expression of choice, or the total recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「投票、票数」，是选举里的单个动作或总票数。

entries.definition: The paper or system used to cast a vote, or the voting itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选票、无记名投票」，指投票用的纸或方式。

entries.definition: A direct vote by the public on a single question, not on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公投」，就一个问题而非人选直接投票。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start at a polling station door, then look at the same event from the winner's side and from the older sense of choosing.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从投票站门口出发，再从当选者一侧与更古老的「选择」义回看同一件事。

normal.en: Election is eligere turned into a noun: one act of picking out.
normal.cn: election 就是 eligere 变成名词：一次「挑出」。

normal.en: A general election fills many seats on one day.
normal.cn: general election 在一天里填满许多席位。

normal.en: From the winner's chair, the election is a personal event.
normal.cn: 坐在当选者的椅子上，election 是一件私人的事。

normal.en: In formal prose, an election can be any deliberate choice.
normal.cn: 在正式文章里，an election 可以指任何慎重的选择。

normal.en: The whole family keeps the same root: elect, election, elector, electoral.
normal.cn: 整族词共用一个词根：elect、election、elector、electoral。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of names pinned beside a door.
abstract.cn: 想象门边钉着一张写满名字的纸。

abstract.en: The same sheet is a public process, a private triumph, or a quiet decision.
abstract.cn: 同一张纸既是公共过程、私人胜利，也可以是一次安静的决定。

abstract.en: Election is a crowd doing the work of one hand.
abstract.cn: election 是一群人在做一只手所做的事。

examples.en: The election result came before midnight.
examples.cn: 选举结果在午夜前出来了。

examples.en: Her election to the board surprised no one.
examples.cn: 她当选董事，没人感到意外。

examples.en: He made a deliberate election to stay silent.
examples.cn: 他有意选择了保持沉默。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of election: the voting process, the fact of being chosen, and any formal choice.
sensesIntro.cn: election 的三个义项：投票过程、当选这一事实，以及正式场合的「选择」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a list of names pinned beside a polling station door.
core.cn: 核心意象：投票站门边钉着一张写满名字的纸。

branches.en: THE MACHINERY: the whole voting process with its rules.
branches.cn: 机器线：带规则的一整套投票过程。

branches.en: THE WIN: the same event seen from the chosen side.
branches.cn: 当选线：从被选中者一侧看同一件事。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: any deliberate choice, in formal prose.
branches.cn: 古义线：正式文章里任何慎重的选择。

branches.en: TWO SIDES: process and outcome are one act named twice.
branches.cn: 两面线：过程与结果，是同一个动作的两种叫法。

branches.cn: 词根线：投票与选择本是同一种「挑出」。

intro.en: Election is the Latin -io noun of elect; English adds -or, -al, -ate and -eer to build the family.

scene: 雨夜里水壶的开关一跳，壶身很快就响了。The electric kettle switched itself off with a click.

senses.title: Of electricity itself
senses.definition: relating to electricity as a physical force, as in current, charge or field
senses.definitionCN: 指作为物理力量的电，如电流、电荷、电场
senses.example: The electric charge built up on the dry cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的布上积聚起了电荷。

senses.whyCN: electric 来自琥珀，摩擦后会吸东西；这个词最初指的就是那股力量本身。

senses.title: Working by electricity
senses.definition: of a machine or device, driven by electricity rather than by fuel or by hand
senses.definitionCN: 指机器或设备，由电力而非燃料或人力驱动
senses.example: The electric kettle switched itself off with a click.
senses.exampleCN: 那只电水壶咔一声自动断电。
senses.why: Once the force had a name, anything running on it was simply described with the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这股力量一旦有了名字，任何靠它运转的东西就用同一个形容词来描述。

senses.title: Tense with excitement
senses.definition: filled with a tense, exciting feeling, as if a current were running through it
senses.definitionCN: 充满紧张兴奋的感觉，仿佛有电流穿过
senses.example: The hall went electric when the band walked on.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队一上台，整个大厅就沸腾了。
senses.why: A shock runs through the body, so a crowd in suspense is described as carrying the same current.
senses.whyCN: 电击会穿过身体，于是屏息的人群也被说成带着同一股电流。

intro.en: Electric was coined in the seventeenth century from Latin electrum, amber, from Greek elektron, because rubbed amber attracts light objects.
intro.cn: electric 是十七世纪由拉丁语 electrum（琥珀）造出，源自希腊语 elektron，因为摩擦过的琥珀会吸起轻物。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the fossil resin that first showed the effect.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，就是最先显现这种效应的树脂化石。

items.en: Latin kept electrum for amber and for a pale gold alloy.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 electrum 指琥珀，也指一种淡金色的合金。

items.en: Seventeenth-century scientists formed electricus for the force shown by rubbed amber.
items.cn: 十七世纪科学家造出 electricus，指摩擦琥珀所显现的那股力。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective and applied it first to bodies that attract.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，最初用于会吸引轻物的物体。

items.en: Industry widened it to machines, and writers stretched it to excitement.
items.cn: 工业把它扩展到机器，作家又把它拉向情绪上的激动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electricity family; the near-meaning group separates electrical, electronic and electrifying.
note.cn: 形近组收 electricity 词族；近义组区分 electrical、electronic 与 electrifying。

entries.definition: Relating to electricity as a system or field of engineering, rather than to one device.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「与电有关的、电气的」，指系统或工程，而非单个器具。

entries.definition: The energy carried by moving charges, or the supply of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电；电力」。

entries.definition: A person who installs and repairs electrical wiring.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电工」。

entries.definition: To charge with electricity, or to thrill suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使带电；使震惊」。

entries.definition: Working by controlling tiny charged particles in circuits, as computers do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电子的」，靠控制电路中的带电微粒工作。

entries.definition: Extremely exciting; the feeling sense pushed to its strongest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极其震撼的」，把情绪义推到最强。

entries.definition: Driven by a stated source, as in battery-powered.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「以……为动力的」，需说明动力来源。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with amber and a spark, then run the same current through kettles and through a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从琥珀与火花出发，再让同一股电流通过水壶与人群。

normal.en: Electric comes from amber: rub it and it pulls threads toward it.
normal.cn: electric 来自琥珀：摩擦之后它会把细线吸过来。

normal.en: Electric names the force; electrical names the system built around it.
normal.cn: electric 指那股力本身；electrical 指围绕它建立的系统。

normal.en: An electric kettle has a plug; an electrical fault has a cause.
normal.cn: electric kettle 有插头；electrical fault 有原因。

normal.en: A hall can go electric without a single wire.
normal.cn: 大厅可以一根电线也没有却「带电」。

normal.en: Electronic is one step further: not just current, but circuits controlling it.
normal.cn: electronic 再进一步：不只是电流，而是控制电流的电路。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip an inch from a door handle, a spark about to jump.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖离门把手一寸，火花就要跳过去。

abstract.en: The same jump can power a kettle or run through a waiting audience.
abstract.cn: 同一次跳跃可以带动水壶，也可以穿过等待的观众。

abstract.en: Electric is energy looking for somewhere to go.
abstract.cn: electric 就是一股急着找去处的能力。

examples.en: The electric charge built up on the dry cloth.
examples.cn: 干燥的布上积聚起了电荷。

examples.en: The electric kettle switched itself off with a click.
examples.cn: 那只电水壶咔一声自动断电。

examples.en: The hall went electric when the band walked on.
examples.cn: 乐队一上台，整个大厅就沸腾了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊莱克垂克」——指尖碰到门把手，啪地跳出火花

root: 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」→ 拉丁语 electrum → 近代拉丁语 electricus；因摩擦琥珀会吸轻物，十七世纪以此命名「电」这股力。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of electric: the physical force itself, devices driven by it, and a mood charged like a current.
sensesIntro.cn: electric 的三个义项：电这股物理力量本身、靠它驱动的器具，以及像电流一样紧绷的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spark jumping from a fingertip to a door handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一簇火花从指尖跳到门把手上。

branches.en: THE FORCE: current, charge and field as physics names them.
branches.cn: 力量线：物理学所说的电流、电荷与电场。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: a kettle or car that runs on that force.
branches.cn: 器具线：靠这股力运转的水壶或汽车。

branches.en: THE MOOD: a crowd charged like a wire.
branches.cn: 情绪线：人群像导线一样带电。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY: the force and the things it drives are one circuit.
branches.cn: 供给线：力量与它驱动的东西是同一条回路。

branches.en: THE SWITCH: a device turns on, and so does a room.
branches.cn: 开关线：器具被打开，房间也被打开。

intro.en: Electric is a scientific coinage on Greek amber; English adds -ity, -al, -ian, -fy and -onic.
intro.cn: electric 是建立在希腊语「琥珀」上的科学造词；英语再加 -ity、-al、-ian、-fy 与 -onic。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are recorded; electricus is a modern scientific formation, not an ancient word.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 均有记录；electricus 是近代科学造词，不是古语。

items.example: It is the ultimate source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个词族的最终来源。

items.example: It carried the Greek word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: 它把希腊词带入拉丁语。

items.example: It was coined in the seventeenth century.
